text:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — finalizing launch tradeoffs doc. Need fast decisions on SLA tiers, pricing backstop, and support routing by EOD Friday.
Dinesh (Eng): I ran final perf on the 8k seq profile for hosted: p50 60ms, p95 220ms, p99 420ms.
Lia - Support: 220ms p95 is a non-starter for a few enterprise pilots — they asked for ~100ms p95.
Jordan S: Dedicated/reserved pools can hit ~90–110ms p95 but cost goes up ~2x. Also longer tail stability is better in ded.
Maya (PM): Proposal: keep hosted SLA at 200ms p95, and offer an "Enterprise Reserved" SLA at 100ms p95 behind Dedicated with a price uplift and contract terms. Thoughts?
Dinesh (Eng): Agree in principle. Caveat: quantized 4-bit variants sometimes show quality regressions (~5–12% on our eval set). We need a quality guardrail and explicit doc language.
Lia - Support: If we promise 100ms SLA, oncall expectations change. Suggest paging threshold: incidents affecting >=5% of requests for >2 minutes. Ops/coverage needs to be explicit.
Jordan S: We can add a graceful fallback: if p95 to a model variant exceeds baseline by 110% for 2m, auto-route to fallback variant (higher-precision) + flag in telemetry. That reduces user-visible errors but increases cost.
Maya (PM): Actionable decisions I want to lock: hosted SLA = 200ms p95 (public pricing); enterprise reserved = 100ms p95 + uplift; fallback behaviour + quality disclaimers in docs; paging threshold as Lia suggested. Any blockers?
Dinesh (Eng): Implementation notes: runtime needs request-level SLA tags so we can report per-customer p95/p99 and attribute cost. Also add a model-quality label in model catalog for "quantization-risk" with a short explanation.
Jordan S: Telemetry reqs: per-route p50/p95/p99, error-rate, fallback-rate, cost-per-1M-tokens, and histograms by sequence length. Need retention plan for 90d hot metrics + 1y aggregated.
Lia - Support: Docs checklist for me: customer-facing SLA text, sample incidents + expected credits, support triage playbook, FAQ on fallback/quality, and handoff to CSMs. I'll draft and share by Tue.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started for release/redwood-inference-v1 -> 12 hosts :rocket:
Dinesh (Eng): Also want an eval gating rule: any new quantized variant must pass the "critical prompt" suite within a 2% degradation threshold or be marked non-default for production routes.
Maya (PM): Good — include that in the launch acceptance matrix as a hard gate. We should also specify billing backstop: if a fallback imposes >15% additional token cost vs expected, billable credits apply or we auto-notify customer with opt-in for fallback.
Jordan S: We can compute projected extra-cost in real time; infra will push a billing alert signal. Need product to define the credit rules.
Lia - Support: For customer comms, we need a simple one-pager: what the tiers mean, when fallback can happen, and who to contact. I'll draft with legal.
Maya (PM): Owners: Lia -> support runbook + FAQ; Jordan -> telemetry + paging thresholds; Dinesh -> runtime tags + eval gates; I'll update acceptance matrix, SLA language, and pricing uplift proposal and ping legal.
Dinesh (Eng): I'll add an Optimize suggestion to default-off risky quantization for enterprise customers unless they opt in.
Jordan S: I'll open infra tickets for retention and histogram pipelines.
Maya (PM): OK locking this as the working decision. I'll update the roadmap doc and mark the launch checklist items with owners/ETA. If no objections, I'll file the final acceptance PR tomorrow morning.
Lia - Support: No objections — will start drafting now.
Dinesh (Eng)::+1:
Jordan S:+1:
Maya (PM): Thanks team — I'll follow up with the updated doc and the PR link.
